article_title: Multifunctional Properties of BMAP-18 and Its Aliphatic Analog against Drug-Resistant Bacteria

mechanism_claims.claim_text: BMAP-18 and BMAP-18-FL permeabilize membranes of the resistant test bacteria under PI uptake/FACScan at 1x MIC, with different MRSA/MDRPA strengths.
direct_assay_types: propidium iodide uptake by FACScan flow cytometry
mechanism_claims.evidence_notes: The paper reports PI-shift percentages for MRSA and MDRPA after peptide exposure at 1x MIC; melittin and buforin-2 are controls.
mechanism_claims.strength_notes: Direct cell-assay evidence for membrane permeabilization; it does not define pore architecture or exclude intracellular effects.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Both peptides bind bacterial plasmid DNA in the gel-retardation assay, with BMAP-18 showing inhibition up to 2 µM and BMAP-18-FL up to 8 µM.
direct_assay_types: E. coli pBR322 plasmid DNA gel-retardation assay
mechanism_claims.evidence_notes: DNA and peptides were co-incubated with pBR322 before agarose gel electrophoresis.
mechanism_claims.strength_notes: Direct in-vitro DNA-binding evidence; intracellular DNA targeting in live bacteria remains an inferred downstream possibility, not a separately proven cellular target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The supplementary SYTOX green assay did not show substantial S. aureus SYTOX influx for either peptide compared with melittin, limiting a simple immediate membrane-lysis interpretation.
direct_assay_types: SYTOX green uptake assay in S. aureus KCTC 1621
mechanism_claims.evidence_notes: Supplementary PDF was opened from the local ZIP; Figure S2 and Method S1 describe no significant SYTOX green entry relative to melittin.
mechanism_claims.strength_notes: This is a boundary condition: PI uptake and DNA binding support membrane/intracellular interaction, while SYTOX does not support broad immediate lysis in this assay.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: BMAP-18-FL shows stronger LPS binding and suppresses LPS-stimulated inflammatory cytokine readouts in RAW 264.7 cells more strongly than BMAP-18.
mechanism_claims.evidence_notes: The paper reports dose-dependent LPS binding, stronger BMAP-18-FL LPS binding, FITC-LPS suppression/binding patterns, and lower cytokine expression for BMAP-18-FL even at 4 µM.
mechanism_claims.strength_notes: Direct immunomodulatory assay evidence; do not restate it as antibacterial killing mechanism.

mechanism_summary: Mechanism review supports membrane permeabilization, in-vitro DNA binding, and BMAP-18-FL immunomodulatory LPS/cytokine effects, while preserving the SYTOX green limiting result.
absence_and_boundary_notes: No direct pore-architecture, receptor-binding structural model, or intracellular target validation beyond plasmid DNA gel binding is reported.
Biofilm eradication is treated as activity evidence rather than a mechanistic target claim.
Anti-inflammatory LPS/cytokine effects are immunomodulatory mechanism evidence and are not converted into antibacterial killing mechanism.
